cohort: A total of 100 patients in active labor were enrolled, with 50 having normal CTG tracings and 50 having abnormal CTG tracings.
finding: Abnormal CTG tracings are strongly associated with adverse pregnancy and neonatal outcomes, including higher rates of cesarean section, low Apgar scores, NICU admissions, and low birth weight.
mod_finding: Patients with abnormal CTG tracings had a significantly higher rate of cesarean sections (68% vs. 44%) compared to those with normal tracings.
cross-section timing: During labor and early neonatal period
